cards.heading: The recovery timeline
cards.body: Days 1–3: hardest, peak withdrawal. Days 4–14: sleep disruption, mood swings, appetite changes. Week 3–4: most symptoms ease. Month 2+: dopamine baseline restores, energy and focus return.

cards.question: When does natural dopamine production typically start to restore after quitting?
cards.explanation: Full dopamine restoration usually takes 4–8 weeks. Some people notice improved mood and motivation sooner, but the full recovery continues for months.

cards.heading: Sleep will come back
cards.body: THC suppresses REM sleep. After quitting, vivid dreams and disrupted sleep are normal — your brain is recalibrating. It typically normalises within 3–4 weeks.

cards.statement: Vivid dreams after quitting cannabis are a sign something is wrong.
cards.explanation: Vivid dreams are actually a sign of recovery. THC suppresses REM sleep — the dreaming phase. As REM returns, dreams become vivid. This is healthy.

cards.prompt: Which part of recovery are you most looking forward to — better sleep, more energy, clearer thinking, or something else? Why?
